identity.title: Investigating star-formation activity towards the southern H II region RCW 42
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: The star-forming activity in the HII region RCW 42 is investigated using multiple wavebands, from near-infrared to radio wavelengths.
Two millimetre emission cores of masses $380$ and $390$ M$_\odot$ towards the radio emission peak have been identified towards C1 from the ALMA map at 1.4 mm.

evidence.quote: Located at a distance of 5.8 kpc, this southern region has a bolometric luminosity of 1.8 $\times$ 10$^6$ L$_{\odot}$.

question.value: What is the extent of star-formation activity and the relative evolutionary stages of clumps in the molecular cloud associated with the southern HII region RCW 42?

evidence.quote: Whether all the clumps in the molecular cloud associated with the HII region, are actively forming stars or whether there exist clumps that are still quiescent is what we are interested in investigating.

Our specific goals in the current work are (a) to probe the molecular cloud using dust emission and to estimate the properties (eg. column density, temperature), and (b) study the clumps in the region and the relative evolutionary stages of various clumps using star-formation tracers.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA$\#$2019.1.00195.L.
Two millimetre emission cores of masses $380$ and $390$ M$_\odot$ towards the radio emission peak have been identified towards C1 from the ALMA map at 1.4 mm.
We used the pipeline reduced continuum image from the archive in the frequency band 216.90 - 220.97 GHz.
The snapshot observations (120s) of central region of RCW 42 have been carried out as part of the ALMAGAL survey (proposal code 2019.1.00195.6) on Oct 06, 2019, using the 7m array configuration.

analysis_steps.goal: Identify 1.4 mm continuum cores in clump C1 and derive their masses

method.value: Run Clumpfind on the archival ALMA 1.4 mm continuum image towards C1 to identify cores MM1 and MM2, then compute core masses assuming optically thin thermal dust emission.

evidence.quote: We have identified two cores within clump C1 (Fig. [6](#cont1)), using the algorithm Clumpfind.
We have estimated the masses of the cores assuming that the emission is optically thin at this frequency.
A threshold of 0.15 Jy/beam and a contour spacing of 7 mJy/beam have been used to identify the dusty cores.

assumptions.value: optically thin emission at 1.4 mm, dust temperature = 38 K, gas-to-dust ratio = 100, opacity per cloud mass = 0.3 cm^2/g for beta = 2 (or gas-to-dust ratio = 150 and beta = 1.8)

evidence.quote: To obtain these estimates, we have considered the gas-to-dust ratio of 100, and opacity per cloud mass of 0.3 cm$^2$/g, using the relation given by (cite: 1983QJRAS..24..267H) for $\beta=2$.
The temperature of 38 K is adopted from the dust temperature map.
Using the opacity relation from (cite: 2013IAUS..292...19T) for $\beta=1.8$ with gas-to-dust ratio of 150, we estimate the dust masses to be 250 and 260 M$_\odot$, respectively.

validation.value: Recalculated core masses with alternative opacity law (beta = 1.8 and gas-to-dust ratio = 150)

analysis_steps.goal: Construct H2 column density and dust temperature maps and identify molecular clumps

method.value: Convolve and regrid Herschel 70-350 um maps to the 500 um resolution (36.9'') and pixel size (14''), subtract background, fit pixel-by-pixel modified blackbody SEDs, and run Clumpfind on the column density map to identify clumps C1-C5 and compute their masses, luminosities, and evolutionary stages.

evidence.quote: We carry out a pixel-to-pixel greybody fitting of the high resolution *Herschel* images and construct line-of-sight averaged molecular hydrogen column density and dust temperature maps.
In order to do this, the 70 - 350 $\mu$m images are first convolved and regridded to the lowest resolution (36.9$''$) and pixel size (14$''$) corresponding to the 500 $\mu$m image.
To ascertain the properties of higher density structures in the cloud, we use the algorithm Clumpfind (cite: 1994ApJ...428..693W) on the column density map.

key_parameters.value: Clumpfind threshold = 5 sigma (4.1e21 cm^-2), contour spacing = 3 sigma (sigma = 8.2e20 cm^-2)

evidence.quote: In the present case, we select a threshold level of $5\sigma$ that corresponds to $N(\mathrm{H_2}) = 4.1\times10^{21}$ cm$^{-2}$, and a contour spacing of $3\sigma$ for the detection of clumps, where $\sigma = 8.2\times10^{20}$ cm$^{-2}$.

assumptions.value: mean molecular weight mu = 2.86, kappa_nu = 0.1 cm^2/g at 250 um, gas-to-dust ratio = 100, beta = 2.0, flux uncertainties = 15%

evidence.quote: $\mu$ is taken to be 2.86 assuming a gas composition of 70% molecular hydrogen by mass (cite: 2010A&A...518L..92W).
We have considered $\kappa_\nu\sim0.1$ cm$^2$/g at 250 $\mu$m, uncertain upto a factor of 2 (cite: 1983QJRAS..24..267H) for a gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100.
We considered the dust emissivity index, $\beta$ equal to 2.0 and assumed flux uncertainties of $\sim15\%$ in the bands (cite: 2009A&A...504..415S),2013A&A...551A..98L.
The best fits were obtained using non-linear least-squares Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm.

validation.value: Repeated pixel-to-pixel SED fitting with alternative opacity (6.8e-3 cm^2/g at 1.2 mm, gas-to-dust ratio 150, beta = 1.8)

evidence.quote: We have, therefore, also considered a cloud opacity of $6.8\times10^{-3}$ cm$^2$g$^{-1}$ at 1.2 mm considering a gas-to-dust mass ratio of $\sim150$ (cite: 2013IAUS..292...19T) and a value of dust emissivity index $\beta=1.8$ determined from Galactic plane emission (cite: 2011A&A...536A..25P).

Based on the GMRT and Parkes images, we estimate the spectral index of RCW 42 as $-0.03\pm0.04$.
The average electron density across the entire region is $\sim70$ cm$^{-3}$.

results_numeric.quantity: Total gas mass of the 5 clumps (beta = 2, gas-to-dust = 100)

evidence.quote: The clumps have mass in the range ${2200-4000}$ M$_\odot$, and the total mass of the clumps is $1.6\times10^4$ M$_\odot$.
As mentioned earlier, the values estimated in this way are uncertain to a factor of 2, and therefore, the column densities and masses of clumps derived are uncertain upto $\sim50$% of their values.
The luminosities of the clumps lie in the range ${90-300\times10^3}$ L$_\odot$, and the total luminosities of the clumps is ${8.7\times10^5}$ L$_\odot$.

findings_qualitative.value: All five dust clumps (C1-C5) in RCW 42 are in an active or evolved stage of star formation and lie in the envelope-clearing phase on the mass-luminosity diagram.

evidence.quote: The clumps are investigated for their evolutionary stages based on association with various star-formation tracers, and we find that all the clumps are in active/evolved stage.
In addition, the positions of these clumps in the M-L diagram indicate that all these clumps are in the envelope clearing phase.

findings_qualitative.value: An extended green object, EGO G274.0649-01.1460, is identified towards I-09230 in clump C3 and is associated with elongated radio emission indicative of an ionized jet/outflow.

evidence.quote: We refer to this source as EGO G274.0649–01.1460 in this work.
It has radio emission with elongated morphology that is associated with extended green object EGO G274.0649–01.1460, suggesting the presence of high mass protostellar outflow(s) within C3.

claims.hypothesis: Whether all the clumps in the molecular cloud associated with RCW 42 are actively forming stars or whether there exist quiescent clumps.
claims.experiment: Identified 5 dust clumps (C1-C5) from Herschel column density maps using Clumpfind and examined their association with radio continuum, Spitzer 8 um, WISE 22 um, NIR YSO/OB candidates, and their position on the mass-luminosity diagram.
claims.result: All 5 clumps are associated with radio emission, infrared star-formation tracers, and lie in the envelope clearing phase of the M-L diagram, with masses of 2200-4000 M_sun and luminosities of 90-300 x 10^3 L_sun.
claims.finding: All 5 clumps in RCW 42 are in an active or evolved evolutionary phase with no quiescent clumps remaining.

evidence.quote: Whether all the clumps in the molecular cloud associated with the HII region, are actively forming stars or whether there exist clumps that are still quiescent is what we are interested in investigating.
All the 5 dust clumps identified in the region are either in active or evolved phase. This implies that RCW 42 is in a relatively advanced evolutionary phase.

claims.hypothesis: Clump C1 towards the radio peak hosts dense millimetre cores associated with massive star formation.
claims.experiment: Analyzed the archival ALMA 1.4 mm continuum map towards I-09227 in clump C1 using Clumpfind.
claims.result: Identified two millimetre cores, MM1 and MM2, separated by 7.7'' (~0.2 pc) with masses of 380 and 390 M_sun (or 250 and 260 M_sun for beta = 1.8).
claims.finding: Clump C1 contains two massive dusty cores near the northern lobe of ionized gas emission associated with UCHII regions.

evidence.quote: We have identified two cores within clump C1 (Fig. [6](#cont1)), using the algorithm Clumpfind.
The masses are quite similar: 380 and 390 M$_\odot$ for MM1 and MM2, respectively.
The cores MM1 and MM2 lie close to the northern lobe of ionized gas emission.

why_this_data.value: ALMA archive data were used to examine high-resolution cold dust emission towards the peak of the molecular cloud (I-09227 / C1), while GMRT, Herschel, Spitzer, and 2MASS probed the ionized gas, molecular cloud dust, and young stellar objects across multiple scales.

evidence.quote: The high resolution cold dust emission towards the peak of the molecular cloud is examined using data from ALMA archive.
In the present work, we examine this region at radio, infrared and submillimeter wavelengths.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: ALMA spectral line cubes were not used because the noise is very high in the 120s snapshot observations.

evidence.quote: We have not considered the associated line emission from spectral cubes as the noise is very high in the snapshot observations.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: T100 balloon-borne flux densities were excluded from the pixel-by-pixel dust temperature and column density fitting due to lower resolution and sensitivity compared to Herschel.

evidence.quote: For this analysis, we did not include the T100 flux densities as the images are of lower resolution and sensitivity compared to the *Herschel* images.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: SUMSS 843 MHz data were excluded from the radio spectral index fit because it is a snapshot image providing only a lower limit.

evidence.quote: SUMSS data at 843 MHz is not considered for the analysis as the image is a snapshot and the estimated flux density (18.3 Jy) is therefore a lower limit.

limitations_admitted.value: GMRT 1280 MHz flux density and electron density values are lower limits because the largest observable angular scale (~8') is smaller than the region size (~12'), missing ~28% of the flux.

evidence.quote: We note that the flux density at 1280 MHz is a lower limit as the largest angular scales that can be mapped at this frequency is $\sim8'$, which is smaller than the size of the region measured at 610 MHz ($\sim12'$).
It is to be noted that these values represent lower limits as the large scale flux is not well sampled at 1280 MHz.

limitations_admitted.value: Derived column densities and clump masses are uncertain by up to ~50% (factor of 2) due to uncertainties in dust opacity kappa_nu and emissivity index beta.

evidence.quote: As mentioned earlier, the values estimated in this way are uncertain to a factor of 2, and therefore, the column densities and masses of clumps derived are uncertain upto $\sim50$% of their values.

limitations_admitted.value: Spitzer 8 um and WISE 22 um images are saturated towards the bright central region/C1, and high nebulosity limits point-source extraction near the radio peak.

evidence.quote: While the 8 $\mu$m image is saturated, the 5.8 $\mu$m emission shows bright nebulous emission over the entire region.
The emission towards C1 is saturated.
